sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- coalition] Saudi air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles fired by the Ansar Allah toward Riyadh on Sunday; earlier on Sunday a ballistic missile targeting the Eastern Province was also intercepted. Saudi Civil Defence issued 'potential danger' alerts for Riyadh City and Najran Province, then lifted them shortly afterwards. [COUNTED -- coalition via Arab News] At least 15 ballistic and cruise missiles and UAVs have been intercepted or destroyed across the Kingdom in November. [CONTEXT -- Arab News] On Saturday air defences destroyed a cruise missile launched toward the Riyadh Region; on Nov 2 two drones and a ballistic missile targeted Riyadh and the southern region; King Khalid International Airport suspended operations in October after attacks that killed and wounded civilians. [UNVERIFIED HOUTHI CLAIM -- separate, Saturday] Ansar Allah spokesman Yahya Saree claimed six operations on Saturday targeting King Khalid International Airport, Aramco oil storage/distillation tower in Riyadh, Aramco Khurais, Pumping Station No. 8 Dawadmi, a National Guard camp in Najran and border positions; Saudi Arabia has NOT confirmed damage from those claimed strikes (recorded Nov 7 at 2100-01). The Ansar Allah have NOT claimed a Sunday launch.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct publisher families carry the coalition's Sunday intercept announcement: Al Jazeera liveblog (05:45 GMT), Arab News (published 03:26Z, updated 05:47Z), Roya News (single ballistic missile toward northern Riyadh, timestamp not exposed). Crypto Briefing (05:38Z) also carries it but has NO declared tier and does not count. The intercept itself is the coalition's own claim -- no independent visual confirmation; the Ansar Allah have not claimed a Sunday launch. Saree's Saturday six-operations damage claims remain unverified.
sections.what_disputed: No Ansar Allah claim for a Sunday launch exists; Saree's Saturday six-operations claim of hits on Riyadh airport and Aramco facilities is unverified and Saudi Arabia has not confirmed damage. No casualties or damage reported from Sunday's intercepts. Precedent for count divergence: Oct 29, the coalition confirmed 2 Riyadh intercepts while AFP journalists in the capital heard 8 explosions. No independent (non-coalition) confirmation of the intercepts.
sections.why_matters: Riyadh under fire again -- second day running, the capital's skies light up: two ballistic missiles at Riyadh, one at the Eastern Province, alerts in Riyadh and Najran. The coalition counts 15 missiles stopped this month -- but the Ansar Allah keep launching.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Arab News published 2026-11-08T03:26:09Z = 07:26 , inside the 0800 window but missed by the 0800 scan; AJ liveblog entry 05:45 GMT = 09:45 , IN-WINDOW) -- Saudi-led coalition intercepts 2 Ansar Allah ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh on Sunday; earlier a missile toward the Eastern Province was also intercepted; Civil Defence 'potential danger' alerts for Riyadh City and Najran lifted minutes later; coalition says at least 15 missiles/UAVs intercepted across the Kingdom in November

totw_analysis: Our read: Riyadh under fire again -- second day running, the capital's skies light up: two ballistic missiles at Riyadh, one at the Eastern Province, alerts in Riyadh and Najran. The coalition counts 15 missiles stopped this month -- but the Ansar Allah keep launching. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Saudi shield holding -- or is the capital now a routine target? Intercepts prove the defence works, or prove the Ansar Allah can strike Riyadh at will.
